item.description:

Status: Roadmap

Use the No auto assignment method for queues in Copilot Service admin center when you want routed conversations to remain unassigned after they enter a queue. Instead of being assigned automatically, conversations stay in the queue until a service representative picks them up from their Inbox or a supervisor assigns them manually. This assignment method supports a pick-based work distribution model, giving supervisors and service representatives greater control over how work is handled. Unlike the push-based model used by other out-of-the-box assignment methods, which automatically assign conversations based on representative availability and capacity, the no auto assignment method allows teams to review incoming work and decide who should handle it. This approach is well suited for organizations that prefer manual oversight, specialized work selection, or supervisor-managed assignments. Business Value: Improve operational control and consistency by enabling service representative-led work distribution. Conversations remain available in the queue until manually assigned by supervisors or picked by representatives, helping teams handle specialized, regulated, or sensitive interactions effectively. item.title: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Project Operations: Optimize Project Operations - Track real project progress from field execution
item.description:
Product: Microsoft 365 Copilot
Status: Roadmap
Importance: low

This feature enhances Dynamics 365 Project Operations by extending its native work breakdown structure effort tracking to include approved time captured in Field Service when the Field Service and Project Operations integration is enabled and time flows in at the project task level. Approved Field Service time now contributes directly to task-level WBS execution metrics in Project Operations when time is captured against a project task. Task metrics such as effort completed, effort remaining, percent complete, estimate at completion, and schedule variance are calculated using approved field labor under the same native project rules used for time entered directly in Project Operations. Because these calculations occur at the leaf task level, their impact rolls up automatically to summary tasks and the project root. Effort tracking views, reprojections, and project-level status indicators reflect real execution in the field, rather than inferred progress or manual reconciliation. Project managers can assess delivery health, forecast outcomes, and identify schedule risk using execution metrics grounded in approved field work. This enhancement doesn't introduce new execution logic or formulas. It enables existing Project Operations WBS effort tracking behavior to include Field Service execution when time is captured against project tasks. This feature is only available when the Field Service and Project Operations integration is enabled. Business Value: When field technicians complete work tied to a project task, you see that progress reflected immediately in your project health metrics. Approved Field Service time flows directly into task-level work breakdown structure (WBS) tracking in Dynamics 365 Project Operations, so effort completed, percent complete, estimate at completion (EAC), and schedule variance stay accurate without manual reconciliation. item.title: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Speed up processing with Known Senders in Payables Agent
item.description:
Product: Microsoft 365 Copilot
Status: Roadmap
Importance: low

This feature introduces email review policy and a Known Senders list page to give accounts payable teams more control over which incoming emails require human approval before the Payables Agent processes them. A new Email review field in the Payables Agent setup lets administrators choose when incoming emails require human approval. The following options are available: Always: Every email requires approval, regardless of the sender. Never: No emails require approval. Only if untrusted (recommended): Only emails from senders who aren't on the list of known senders require review. This is the recommended setting for most organizations. Administrators must explicitly select an option before they start to monitor the email inbox. To ensure that they make an active decision, a default isn't preselected for the field. Every known sender is subject to a setting that sets the review policy for the specific sender. When you set the email review policy to Manage per sender , the agent evaluates incoming emails in the following order: Invoice is uploaded and not received via email: No review required. Email subfolder is configured: All emails in the monitored subfolder are treated as trusted. No review required. Sender is on the Known Senders list: Action depends on the configured value (Ask, Approve, or Reject). Internal sender (same organization, not on the list): No review required. Internal detection uses email authentication headers (planned to be available in 2026 wave 2, version 29.0.). Administrators can maintain a list of known senders, each with a configured policy: Ask: The email requires human approval. Approve: The agent processes the invoice without review. Reject: The sender is blocked and the attachment isn't processed. To build the list organically, after you review an email and want to continue, the sender is added automatically to the list of known senders, provided that the Manage per sender policy is active. Security telemetry is logged for each auto-addition. This feature is available from the August minor release of 2026 release wave 1. Business Value: Payables Agent processes vendor invoices received by email, but today every incoming email requires supervisor approval before the agent can act on it, unless email review is disabled entirely. item.title: [Roadmap] Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Detect intraday volume spikes with workforce alerts
item.description:
Product: Microsoft 365 Copilot
Status: Roadmap
Importance: low

Supervisors can create volume spike alerts that compare real-time conversation volume with the forecast linked to a shift plan. When volume remains above forecast for the configured number of intervals, selected recipients receive an in-app notification. The capability includes the following features: Administrators can enable workforce alerts in Copilot Service admin center by going to Workforce management > Intraday management > Workforce alerts . Supervisors can create and manage alerts from Workforce alerts in the Copilot Service workspace site map. Each alert references a shift plan and monitors the queues associated with its linked capacity plan. Supervisors can specify the percentage by which actual volume must exceed forecast volume. Supervisors can specify the number of consecutive intervals during which the deviation must continue before an alert is raised. The forecast determines whether an interval is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Supervisors can set an expiration date to limit an alert to a campaign, season, or known event. Supervisors can select one or more notification recipients for each alert. Active alerts are evaluated on a recurring schedule. Notifications are sent when the configured threshold and duration are met. Recipients can select a notification to open the alert details. The details include the queue and alert name, detection time, current and forecast volumes, spike percentage, and an interval-by-interval breakdown. Access and prerequisites An administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from Power Platform admin center. Forecasting and scheduling must be configured. The selected shift plan must have a linked capacity plan and forecast. Real-time conversation data must be available for the monitored queues. Business Value: Contact centers plan staffing based on forecasted demand, but actual demand can change quickly. When conversation volume rises significantly above forecast, queues can grow and service levels can decline before supervisors have time to respond. Workforce alerts help supervisors identify unusual intraday volume changes without continuously monitoring a dashboard. Supervisors define the deviation and duration that represent a volume spike and select who should be notified when those conditions are met. The notification provides information about the spike, including how far actual volume is above forecast and whether the deviation is continuing. Supervisors can use this information to decide whether to shift capacity, offer overtime, or defer offline work while these actions can still help protect the customer experience. This ensures customers are always routed to the best possible outcome, even when direct support is unavailable. Business Value: This capability ensures customers are never left waiting when representatives aren't available. Whether a queue transitions to be out-of-operating hours or all support representatives are logged out, the system proactively routes conversations to configured fallback options such as voicemail, callback, or alternative queues. Organizations benefit from reduced wait times and lower abandonment, improved customer satisfaction during peak load or unexpected staffing gaps, and a more predictable service experience regardless of representative availability. At the same time, this eliminates the need for manual queue draining or extended shifts, helping protect service representative wellbeing while maintaining consistent service levels.
